key_insight: ATLAS is a foundation neural sampler that learns diffusion-based Boltzmann sampling for amorphous materials, enabling efficient generation, estimation, and steering of rugged energy-landscape states.
engineering_relevance: It can reduce expensive sampling and inverse-design costs for glasses and disordered alloys, helping engineers search for compositions and structures with targeted mechanical properties.
method: Equivariant graph neural network parameterizes the reverse diffusion process.
Trained to sample directly from a target energy function across system size, temperature, and composition.
Uses diffusion time reversal for thermodynamic estimation and property steering.
evidence_signal: Across Kob-Andersen, Cu-Zr, and Cr-Co-Ni systems, ATLAS matched reference structural distributions and achieved below 0.2% free-energy error in the low-temperature regime with over 500× fewer energy evaluations.
watch_item: Performance may depend on access to a suitable target energy model and careful validation when transferring to new chemistries or high-dimensional design spaces.
paper_title: ATLAS: A Foundation Neural Sampler for Amorphous Materials
